description: Curated benchmark database of state-of-the-art open-source resources for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and Robotics Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

resources.name: OpenVLA (7B)
resources.summary: An open-source 7B parameter Vision-Language-Action model trained on 970k robot episodes from the Open X-Embodiment dataset. Built on Prismatic VLMs and Llama-2.
resources.description: OpenVLA is a state-of-the-art generalist robot policy that directly outputs discrete action tokens corresponding to 7-DoF robot arm movements (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, gripper). It achieves a 16.5% absolute improvement in task completion over RT-2-X (55B) while being 7x smaller, and supports parameter-efficient fine-tuning via LoRA on consumer GPUs.
resources.authors: Moo Jin Kim, Karl Pertsch, Siddharth Karamcheti, et al. (Stanford, UC Berkeley)
resources.action_space: 7-DoF Delta End-Effector Pose + Gripper (Action Chunking / Auto-regressive)

hardware_requirements.training: 8x NVIDIA A100/H100 (full) or 1x RTX 4090 / A100 (LoRA fine-tuning)

resources.name: Octo (Base & Small)
resources.summary: An open-source generalist robot policy based on transformer diffusion policies, trained on 800k trajectories from Open X-Embodiment.
resources.description: Octo introduces a flexible transformer architecture supporting multi-camera RGB inputs, natural language instructions, and goal images. It uses a diffusion head to predict continuous action chunks (time horizons of 2-8 steps), avoiding action discretization artifacts and enabling high-frequency control (up to 10Hz).
resources.authors: Octo Model Team (Dibya Ghosh, Homer Walke, Karl Pertsch, Kevin Black, et al.)
resources.action_space: Continuous Action Chunks (7-DoF EEF Delta + Gripper)

resources.name: ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers)
resources.summary: State-of-the-art imitation learning policy utilizing a Conditional VAE and Transformer encoder-decoder for bimanual and single-arm manipulation.
resources.description: ACT models human demonstrations with temporal action chunking to mitigate compounding errors. It is the gold standard baseline for fine manipulation tasks (e.g. threading, slotting, folding) using teleoperation setups like ALOHA.
resources.authors: Tony Z. Zhao, Vikash Kumar, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn
resources.action_space: 14-DoF Joint Positions or 7-DoF EEF (Action Chunks of 50-100 steps)

resources.name: Diffusion Policy
resources.summary: Visuomotor policy learning via Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for multimodal robot action distributions.
resources.description: Diffusion Policy formulates robot action generation as a conditional diffusion process over continuous action sequences. Excels at multimodal human behaviors, avoiding mode collapse common in standard MSE-loss regression networks.
resources.authors: Cheng Chi, Siyuan Feng, Yilun Du, Zhenjia Xu, Eric Cousineau, Benjamin Burchfiel, Shuran Song
resources.organization: Columbia University, MIT, Toyota Research Institute

resources.name: π0 (Physical Intelligence Foundation Model)
resources.summary: A 3B parameter physical intelligence foundation model combining flow matching and vision-language pretraining for diverse dexterous tasks.
resources.description: π0 leverages continuous flow matching conditioned on high-capacity vision-language embeddings to execute high-frequency (50Hz) dexterous manipulation across laundry folding, box assembly, and multi-robot coordination.
resources.authors: Physical Intelligence Team (Kevin Black, Noah Brown, Danny Driess, Adnan Esmail, et al.)
resources.action_space: High-frequency Continuous Flow matching (50Hz Joint & Gripper)

resources.name: Prismatic VLMs
resources.summary: Fast, modular, and deeply researched open-source vision-language model training codebase and model zoo powering OpenVLA.
resources.description: Prismatic VLMs explores architectural tradeoffs in vision representations (fusing SigLIP and DINOv2 features) paired with modern language decoders (Llama-2, Mistral, Gemma). Serves as the direct architectural foundation for OpenVLA.
resources.authors: Siddharth Karamcheti, Suraj Nair, Ashwin Balakrishna, Percy Liang, Chelsea Finn
resources.action_space: Text Token Generation / Extendable to Action Tokens

resources.name: PaliGemma / PaliGemma 2
resources.summary: Google's open-weights vision-language model optimized for transfer learning, spatial grounding, and fine-tuning across diverse downstream tasks.
resources.description: Combines a SigLIP-So400m vision encoder with Gemma-2B/9B language models. Exceptional at spatial bounding box generation, object segmentation coordinates, and fine-grained localization, making it an ideal pre-trained backbone for robotics manipulation.
resources.action_space: Coordinate Tokens, Spatial Bounding Boxes, Text

resources.name: Qwen2-VL (2B, 7B, 72B)
resources.summary: State-of-the-art open-source Vision-Language model with dynamic resolution visual tokenization and video understanding capabilities.
resources.description: Features NaViT dynamic resolution processing and 3D visual tokenization, allowing native processing of arbitrary aspect ratios and robot camera video streams. Superior spatial grounding and OCR capabilities make it highly effective for spatial manipulation tasks.
resources.action_space: Bounding Box Tokens, Point Coordinates, Text

hardware_requirements.training: 4x A100 for 7B full tuning, 1x A100 for 2B LoRA

resources.name: Open X-Embodiment (OXE) Dataset
resources.summary: The ImageNet of robotics: 1M+ real-world robot trajectories across 22 different robot embodiments from 34 research labs worldwide.
resources.description: Standardized in RLDS (Reinforcement Learning Dataset Standard) format, OXE provides diverse demonstrations of object manipulation, pick-and-place, tool use, and drawer operations with synchronized camera views, proprioceptive state, and natural language annotations.
resources.authors: Open X-Embodiment Collaboration (UC Berkeley, Stanford, Google DeepMind, CMU, etc.)

resources.name: BridgeData V2
resources.summary: A dataset of 60,000+ diverse robotic manipulation trajectories collected across 24 environments on WidowX arms.
resources.description: Specifically designed for generalizable robotic manipulation with rich scene variation, toy kitchens, real sinks, clutter, and varying lighting conditions. Includes multiple camera views (eye-in-hand and third-person) with verified language task annotations.
resources.authors: Homer Walke, Kevin Black, Abraham Lee, Moo Jin Kim, et al.

resources.name: DROID (Distributed Robot Open Interaction Dataset)
resources.summary: 76,000 demonstration trajectories collected across 564 diverse real-world environments with Franka Panda arms.
resources.description: High-quality manipulation dataset collected in residential homes, offices, labs, and commercial kitchens across North America, Europe, and Asia. Features stereo RGB camera recordings, wrist cameras, high-precision proprioception, and rich natural language task descriptions.
resources.authors: Alexander Khazatsky, Karl Pertsch, Suraj Nair, et al.
resources.organization: DROID Dataset Team (Stanford, UC Berkeley, CMU, etc.)
resources.action_space: 7-DoF Cartesian EEF Velocity / Delta Pose + Gripper

resources.name: ALOHA / Mobile ALOHA Datasets
resources.summary: Fine-grained bimanual mobile manipulation dataset demonstrating complex tasks (cooking, wiping, chair lifting, elevator calling).
resources.description: Recorded with low-cost teleoperation systems using two ViperX arms on a mobile base. Demonstrates that 50 demonstrations per task are sufficient to train co-fine-tuned imitation learning policies with high success rates.
resources.authors: Zipeng Fu, Tony Z. Zhao, Chelsea Finn

resources.name: ManiSkill 3
resources.summary: GPU-parallelized robotics simulation benchmark for articulated object manipulation powered by SAPIEN and Vulkan.
resources.description: ManiSkill 3 provides lightning-fast GPU-parallelized physics simulation (over 30,000+ FPS on a single RTX 4090). It supports heterogeneous robot embodiments (Franka, UR5, ALOHA, Humanoid), complex articulated tasks (door opening, faucet turning, cabinet rearrangement), and out-of-the-box sim-to-real evaluation pipelines.
resources.authors: Stone Tao, Jiayuan Gu, Hao Su, et al.
resources.action_space: Joint Position / Velocity / Cartesian EEF / Torque

hardware_requirements.gpu: NVIDIA GPU with Vulkan ray-tracing support (RTX 3070+ recommended)

resources.name: Isaac Lab (NVIDIA Isaac Sim)
resources.summary: Modular, unified framework for robot learning in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, built on PhysX 5 and RTX GPU acceleration.
resources.description: Isaac Lab (successor to Orbit) enables high-throughput reinforcement learning and imitation learning for robot arms, quadrupeds, humanoids, and mobile manipulators. Features photorealistic sensor rendering, domain randomization, and seamless export to ONNX and ROS 2 for physical hardware deployment.
resources.authors: Mayank Mittal, Kelly Guo, David Hoeller, et al.
resources.action_space: Joint Position / Joint Torques / Operational Space Impedance

hardware_requirements.gpu: NVIDIA RTX 3080/4080/4090 or A100/H100 with Omniverse Isaac Sim

resources.name: SIMPLER Benchmark
resources.summary: Sim-and-Real Evaluated Policy Evaluation benchmark specifically calibrated for generalist robot policies like OpenVLA and RT-1/RT-2.
resources.description: SIMPLER addresses the sim-to-real gap for evaluating generalist manipulation models. It replicates real-world WidowX and Google Robot evaluation environments inside SAPIEN simulation, showing high Pearson correlation (0.8+) between simulated task success and physical robot real-world task success.
resources.authors: Xuanlin Li, Kyle Hsu, Jiayuan Gu, Karl Pertsch, et al.

resources.name: RoboCasa Simulation Environment
resources.summary: Large-scale simulation benchmark of everyday kitchen and household manipulation tasks for generalist robot learning.
resources.description: Built on MuJoCo, RoboCasa provides over 100 kitchen layouts, 2,500+ object assets, and 100+ task categories (e.g. brewing coffee, slicing vegetables, washing dishes). Evaluates models on instruction following and long-horizon multi-step planning.
resources.authors: Soroush Nasiriany, Abhiram Maddukuri, Lance Zhang, Adeet Patel, et al.
resources.action_space: Cartesian EEF Delta + Gripper + Mobile Base Velocity

resources.name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
resources.summary: Hugging Face's official open-source library for state-of-the-art robotics AI models, datasets, and affordable hardware.
resources.description: LeRobot democratizes robotics AI by providing standardized PyTorch implementations of state-of-the-art policies (ACT, Diffusion Policy, TDMPC, OpenVLA integration), dataset formats (Zarr/Parquet on Hugging Face Hub), pre-trained weights, and real-robot hardware build guides (SO-100, Koch v1.1).
resources.authors: Rémi Cadène, Quentin Gallouédec, Simon Alibert, et al.
resources.action_space: Continuous Action Chunking, Joint Angles, EEF

resources.name: Robomimic
resources.summary: A modular framework for robot imitation learning and offline reinforcement learning, developed by Stanford and UT Austin.
resources.description: Robomimic provides reproducible implementations of BC, BC-RNN, HBC, Action-Chunking, Diffusion Policy, and Offline RL algorithms (CQL, IQL). Standardized HDF5 data format with pre-computed sensory observations, observation normalization, and multi-seed evaluation suites.
resources.authors: Ajay Mandlekar, Danfei Xu, Josiah Wong, Soroush Nasiriany, Chelsea Finn, Silvio Savarese
resources.action_space: OSC Pose, Joint Velocity, Joint Position

resources.name: OpenVLA Training & Fine-Tuning Codebase
resources.summary: Official distributed PyTorch training library for pretraining and LoRA fine-tuning 7B parameter VLA models.
resources.description: Features efficient data loading for Open X-Embodiment RLDS datasets, FlashAttention-2, PyTorch FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel), and Hugging Face PEFT LoRA integration. Enables adapting generalist VLA models to new robot embodiments in under 15 minutes on a single consumer GPU.
resources.authors: Moo Jin Kim, Karl Pertsch, Siddharth Karamcheti, et al.
resources.action_space: Discrete Action Tokens (256 bins per DoF)
